cardFeeCalculator.title: Card Fee Calculator
cardFeeCalculator.subtitle: Korean preferential merchant fee rates for H2 2026 (from Aug 14, 2026) · estimate card fees from your annual sales bracket and monthly card sales, and your net cost after the VAT credit

bracket.label: Annual sales bracket
bracket.hint: Based on total annual sales (card and cash, from National Tax Service records). Brackets are reassessed every half-year, and the Credit Finance Association mails notices to eligible merchants.

annual.label: Find bracket by annual sales (optional)
annual.hint: Enter annual sales to pick the bracket automatically.

monthly.label: Monthly card sales
monthly.hint: Amount paid by credit and check cards in one month (VAT included)
monthly.over: Card sales alone come to {card} KRW a year, above the {bracket} bracket limit. Please check your sales bracket.

checkShare.label: Check card share
checkShare.hint: Per month: credit {credit} KRW · check {check} KRW (debit and prepaid cards use the check card rate)

rates.hint: Picking a bracket fills in the H2 2026 preferential rates. If your card company's notice differs, edit them.
rates.hintGeneral: General merchant rates are set per contract by each card company. The default is the published prior-year industry average (annual sales 3B–10B: credit 2.10%, check 1.44%) for reference only, so enter your own rate.

vat.title: VAT credit for card sales (1.3% on 2026 supplies, up to 10M KRW a year)
vat.netNegative: The VAT credit exceeds your card fees by {n} KRW. The credit can’t exceed the VAT you owe for the period (VAT Act Art. 46(1)).
vat.netPositive: Even after the VAT credit, card fees cost you {n} KRW.
vat.proposal: From 2027 supplies, if the government's tax reform bill (1.2%, 5M KRW annual cap, pending in the National Assembly) passes, the credit becomes {credit} KRW and the net cost {net} KRW.
vat.noneCorp: Corporations can't claim this VAT credit (VAT Act Art. 46). Card fees are a straight cost.
vat.noneLarge: Sole proprietors whose prior-year supply value exceeds 1B KRW aren't eligible (VAT Act Art. 46). Pick a bracket of 1B KRW or less to see the credit.
vat.note: Applies to sole proprietors that mainly sell to consumers, such as retail, restaurants and lodging (simplified taxpayers included). Cash receipt sales count too, and any credit above the VAT you owe is not refunded.

share.label: Monthly card sales {monthlyM}M KRW · {bracket} merchant
share.headline: Annual card fees {fee} KRW
share.sub: VAT credit {credit} KRW → net cost {net} KRW
share.text: With {monthlyM}M KRW in monthly card sales ({bracket} merchant), card fees are {monthlyFee} KRW a month and {fee} KRW a year.

actions.vatNote: Opens the VAT calculator's return tab with six months of card sales. Adjust non-card sales and purchases there.

compare.title: If your sales bracket changes
compare.desc: Annual fees by bracket for the same {monthlyM}M KRW monthly card sales and check card share.
compare.up: If annual sales pass {upper} and you become a {next} merchant, you pay {diff} KRW more a year on the same card sales.
compare.top: General is the top bracket. Rates depend on your contract with each card company.
compare.loseCredit: If your prior-year supply value also exceeds 1B KRW, you lose the VAT credit ({credit} KRW a year) as well.
compare.note: The General row uses the industry average as a reference. In December 2024, card companies agreed to freeze for three years the rates of general merchants with annual sales up to 100B KRW whose rates would otherwise rise after the cost review.

newMerchant.title: Refunds for new merchants
newMerchant.desc: A new card merchant pays the general merchant rate until its sales are confirmed. If the next half-yearly review confirms it as a micro or SME merchant, the preferential rate is applied retroactively and the difference is refunded to its card settlement account. Merchants that closed in the meantime are included.
newMerchant.estimate: With {monthlyM}M KRW in monthly card sales, you get back about {refund} KRW per month compared with the general rate (reference: credit {credit}%, check {check}%).
newMerchant.note: The Financial Services Commission announced (Aug 11, 2026) that about 159,000 credit card merchants opened in H1 2026 will be refunded about 61.47B KRW (about 387,000 KRW each on average) by Sep 28, 2026. Check eligibility on the Credit Finance Association's merchant sales lookup (cardsales.or.kr) or with your card company.

tips.title: Good to know
items: Preferential brackets are reassessed every half-year. Notices arrive around February and August, and if your sales grow, your rate can rise from the next half-year.
Check the rate currently applied to you on cardsales.or.kr (merchant fee rate lookup) or by calling the Credit Finance Association (02-2011-0700).
Sub-merchants of payment gateways (PG), such as online shops, and taxi operators also get preferential rates by sales bracket. Ask your PG or transit settlement provider for your rate.
Preferential check card rates are 0.25–0.30%p lower than credit card rates in the same bracket. A higher check card share lowers your effective rate.
Card fees are a business expense, so you can include them as necessary expenses when calculating income tax.
The VAT credit for card sales is 1.3% (up to 10M KRW a year) on supplies through Dec 31, 2026. From 2027 it depends on the tax law the National Assembly passes, so check the year-end amendment.
